newsitem.title: USA: Apple expected to reunite with ad agency Chiat/Day.
newsitem.headline: Apple expected to reunite with ad agency Chiat/Day.

text.p: With a new board, new cash and likely a new message, Apple Computer Inc. will reportedly announce on Friday it is reuniting with the advertising agency that created the highly acclaimed "1984" television commercial.

Published reports said that barring a last-minute snag, the struggling computer maker will name TBWA Chiat/Day in Venice, Calif., a unit of Omnicom Group, to handle its U.S. advertising with billings estimated at $80 million to $90 million.

TBWA Chiat/Day is the successor to Chiat/Day, the agency that created the well-known commercial in 1984 that launched the Apple Macintosh. The television spot, shown during the Super Bowl, portrayed a hammer-wielding woman athlete attacking a giant Orwellian video screen representing numbing conformity.

Apple announced Wednesday that its long-time rival Microsoft Corp. was investing $150 million in the company and that the board of directors was being revamped. The news sent Apple's stock soaring, and at least two brokerages raised their rating on the shares Thursday.
The surprise announcements were made in Boston at the MacWorld Exposition by Apple co-founder Steven Jobs, who is serving as a special adviser to the company.
Jobs had worked with Chiat/Day on development of the "1984" commercial, but by 1986 both were gone and BBDO Worldwide, also part of the Omnicom Group, was handling Apple's advertising.
In June Apple announced it was reviewing its U.S. advertising and BBDO declined to participate.
